classicBeybladePhysics: Classic Plastic Generation physics apply: physical Beyblades stay palm-sized, solid and tip-driven; right-spin and left-spin remain constant; stadium translation is separate from axial rotation; collisions use direct Attack Ring contact with recoil; supernatural energy remains anchored to the visible physical top. Real-world spin-stability lock: angular momentum is the only thing that keeps a free Beyblade balanced on its pointed tip. As RPM approaches zero, precession must widen, the rim or base must touch, and gravity must tip the body onto its side. A non-spinning free top may not remain upright on its tip or freeze in a balanced pose. It may stay level while not spinning only when visibly supported by a hand or fixture, lying flat on a broad surface, or firmly locked to both launcher posts.

The storyboard sheet itself is never visible: no multi-panel grid, split screen, panel borders, divider lines, gutters, white margins, page edges, cropped fragments from adjacent panels, captions, labels, timestamps, or typography.

stadiumMotionLock: Post-landing stadium-motion lock: after the tip's first contact, a spinning Beyblade must continue both axial rotation and visible translation across the bowl. A brief landing skid transitions immediately into a curved orbit governed by tip friction, gravity and the local bowl tangent; on a slope it travels along or down the surface and may precess, climb, descend or deflect, but it never adheres to the slope, freezes in place, or pivots around a glued point. Even a defense-type top traces a tight low-speed orbit or small precessing circle. It may become stationary only after RPM decays, wobble widens, the rim scrapes and the body falls onto its side.
